title: REV Quezon City Half Marathon 2026 Review: RUNRIO Brings a New Brand to the Philippines' Largest City
seo_title: REV QC Half Marathon 2026 Review: Course, Tips & RUNRIO Guide
meta_description: REV Quezon City Half Marathon 2026 review: RUNRIO's new REV-branded race in QC. 21K, 10K, and 5K on December 13. Course expectations, race conditions, and registration guide.
dek: The REV Quezon City Half Marathon marks the arrival of the REV brand — a growing name in Philippine road racing — into Metro Manila's largest and most populous city, with RUNRIO Inc. handling the production. Scheduled for December 13, 2026, the event offers three distances (21K, 10K, 5K) and brings RUNRIO's established race-organisation pedigree to Quezon City's broad avenues, university campuses, and the thousands of runners who already log their weekly kilometres along the UP Diliman Academic Oval.
verdict: The REV Quezon City Half Marathon has one thing going for it that separates it from most provincial Philippine races: RUNRIO Inc. is the organiser. RUNRIO is the country's premier mass-participation race producer — the team behind the National MILO Marathon, the PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series, and dozens of other events that have set the standard for Philippine road racing over the past two decades. When RUNRIO attaches its name to a new brand like REV, the industry pays attention. Quezon City is the ideal venue for this partnership: it is the Philippines' most populous city, home to the UP Diliman Academic Oval (the country's most famous running loop), and well-connected to every corner of Metro Manila via EDSA, Commonwealth Avenue, and the MRT-7 line. The December 13 date falls in the sweet spot of the Philippine running calendar — the typhoon season has wound down, the northeast monsoon is bringing cooler air, and race conditions should be among the best Metro Manila offers all year. The unknowns are real: registration has not yet opened, the specific course route has not been published, and the REV brand itself is still establishing its identity in a market dominated by MILO, PUMA, and the major trilogy series. But the RUNRIO factor means this race is almost certain to be well-produced, safely managed, and worth the entry fee — whenever registration does open. For Metro Manila runners, this is one to put on the calendar now. For runners elsewhere, watch for the course announcement: if RUNRIO secures a route through the UP Diliman campus or along the wide boulevards of the Quezon Memorial Circle area, this could become one of the stronger half marathons on the Philippine calendar.

sections.heading: The REV Brand and the RUNRIO Factor
paragraphs: REV is a growing brand in the Philippine running scene, appearing on race calendars alongside established names like MILO, PUMA, and the various trilogy series [1]. While REV does not yet carry the decades-long heritage of those brands, its partnership with RUNRIO Inc. for the Quezon City half marathon changes the calculus significantly [1].

RUNRIO Inc. — founded by Coach Rio de la Cruz — is the gold standard for Philippine race organisation. The company has produced the National MILO Marathon for years, manages the PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series, and has run events ranging from 5K fun runs to full marathons with tens of thousands of participants [2]. Their hallmarks are consistent: chip timing, well-marked courses, adequate hydration stations, medical support that actually shows up, and a race-day production quality that makes the early-morning alarm clock feel worthwhile [2].

When RUNRIO attaches its operational expertise to a newer brand like REV, it signals that the brand is investing in quality rather than cutting corners. For runners trying to decide whether a race listed on a calendar is worth their Sunday morning, 'organised by RUNRIO' is about as strong a signal as you can get in the Philippine running market [2].

sections.heading: Quezon City: The Philippines' Running Capital
paragraphs: Quezon City is the Philippines' most populous city — home to roughly three million people and the de facto hub of the country's running community [3]. The UP Diliman Academic Oval, a 2.2-kilometre loop shaded by acacia trees inside the University of the Philippines campus, is the most famous running route in the country and the de facto training ground for generations of Filipino runners, from weekend joggers to national-team athletes [3].

Beyond UP Diliman, Quezon City offers wide, multi-lane thoroughfares — Commonwealth Avenue, Quezon Avenue, and the roads surrounding the Quezon Memorial Circle — that are well-suited to hosting a half marathon course with minimal disruption to traffic when properly managed [3]. The city is also the most accessible point in Metro Manila for runners coming from the northern suburbs (Fairview, Novaliches, Caloocan) and from the south via EDSA, making it a natural gathering point for the broader Metro Manila running community [3].

For a half marathon, the ideal course would start and finish near the Quezon Memorial Circle or within the UP Diliman campus, using the wide boulevards for the bulk of the distance and the Academic Oval for a scenic finish. Whether RUNRIO can secure the necessary road closures and permits for such a route remains to be seen — but the geography is promising [1].

sections.heading: December 13: Why the Date Matters
paragraphs: December in Metro Manila is the beginning of the dry season and one of the best times of year to run a road race in the Philippines [4]. The southwest monsoon (habagat), which brings typhoons and heavy rain from June through November, has fully retreated by early December. The northeast monsoon (amihan) takes over, bringing cooler, drier air from the Asian mainland — morning temperatures in Metro Manila during December typically sit in the low-to-mid 20s Celsius, which is as good as Philippine race weather gets [4].

The December 13 date also places the REV QC Half Marathon in a relatively uncrowded window on the Philippine running calendar. The major November races (MILO National Finals, various trilogy finales) are done, and the holiday-season races have not yet begun in earnest [1]. This gives the event breathing room to attract runners who are looking for one last serious race before the Christmas break — or one last chance to hit a year-end PR in favourable conditions [4].

The one note of caution: December in Quezon City can still deliver a hot morning, especially if the race starts at 5:00am or later. The sun rises around 6:10am in December, and by 7:00am the temperature can climb into the high 20s — runners targeting the half marathon distance should plan their pacing around a cool first hour and a steadily warming second hour [4].

sections.heading: Registration, Distances, and What to Expect
paragraphs: As of this writing, registration for the REV Quezon City Half Marathon 2026 has not yet opened [1]. This is typical for RUNRIO-produced events, which tend to announce registration details — including pricing tiers, race-kit inclusions, and venue for kit collection — approximately two to three months before race day [2]. Based on RUNRIO's pricing patterns for comparable Metro Manila half marathons, expect early-bird rates in the PHP 1,200–1,800 range, rising to PHP 1,800–2,500 closer to race day [2].

Three distances are offered: a 21.1K half marathon (the headline event), a 10K, and a 5K [1]. This is the standard RUNRIO distance portfolio and covers everyone from serious half-marathoners to casual runners and families. Race-kit inclusions typically feature a quality event shirt (not the thin cotton that shrinks after one wash), a race bib with timing chip, and a finisher's medal for all categories [2].

Registration, when it opens, will most likely be handled through RUNRIO's official registration platform — typically announced on the RUNRIO Facebook page, the REV brand's social media channels, and the Pinoy Fitness events calendar [1][2]. Metro Manila races organised by RUNRIO frequently sell out their half-marathon slots, so runners who are serious about this event should register early once the window opens [2].

sections.heading: Should You Run the REV Quezon City Half Marathon?
paragraphs: If you live anywhere in Metro Manila or the surrounding provinces (Bulacan, Rizal, Laguna, Cavite): yes, this race should be on your radar for late 2026. The RUNRIO production quality, the accessible Quezon City location, and the December weather combine to make this one of the more promising half marathons on the Philippine calendar — and the entry fee, whatever it turns out to be, will almost certainly represent fair value for a RUNRIO-produced event [1][2].

If you are an international runner or a marathon tourist: hold off on booking flights until the course map and registration details are published. The race has strong fundamentals — RUNRIO, Quezon City, December — but the course route will determine whether this is a genuinely compelling destination race or simply a well-produced local event. If RUNRIO secures a route through UP Diliman and the Quezon Memorial Circle area, it becomes a much more interesting proposition [1].

If you are tracking the REV brand: this race is worth watching as a signal of REV's ambitions. Partnering with RUNRIO for a Metro Manila half marathon is a significant investment — it suggests REV wants to compete in the premium tier of Philippine road racing alongside MILO and PUMA. How this race is produced, promoted, and received will tell us a lot about where REV is headed [2].
